blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jacob had run from home after he tricked his brother Esau. He traveled a long way east, to the land where his mother's people lived. He came to a well in a field and asked the shepherds if they knew a man named Laban. They did. And here came Laban's daughter now.

verses.text: And while he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep: for she kept them.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother’s brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother’s brother.

verses.text: And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He had come all that way by himself, not knowing what he would find. Now he was standing in front of his own family. No wonder he cried.

verses.text: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s brother, and that he was Rebekah’s son: and she ran and told her father.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jacob stayed and worked a month. Then his uncle brought up wages.

verses.text: And Laban said unto Jacob, Because thou art my brother, shouldest thou therefore serve me for nought? tell me, what shall thy wages be?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Leah was tender eyed. Nobody knows for sure what that meant. What is plain is that Jacob only had eyes for her little sister.

verses.text: And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When the seven years were done, Jacob asked for his bride, and Laban threw a wedding feast. But that night Laban brought Leah instead of Rachel. In the dark, under the veil, Jacob did not know.

verses.text: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Church, Jacob once fooled his own father in the dark, pretending to be his older brother. Now he was the one fooled, by a father who swapped the younger for the older. Jacob reaped what he had sown.

verses.text: And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: It is not a happy story. Jacob got tricked. Rachel had to wait. And Leah was given to a man who did not want her, and she knew it.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: But the very next verse says the LORD saw that Leah was not loved. He saw her. She named her sons for what God was doing in her heart, and with her fourth son she said, now I will praise the LORD. His name was Judah. From Judah came King David, and in time, Jesus. Church, the sister nobody picked was never overlooked by God.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Gen 29:9-30, tagged sexual implied (v23 left out); Leah seen by God is v31 and her sons' names vv32-35; Judah to David to Jesus stated without references; 'reaped what he had sown' is Gal 6:7's sense, not a promise.

cultural.note: Leah honoured, never a joke about looks; 'love makes the years short' tied to v20.
